learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan within companies, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Adopt a responsible, organized attitude towards work and be willing to learn, considering the challenge of continuous training.

Apply the strategies of scientific methodology: analyze problematic situations qualitatively and quantitatively, propose hypotheses and solutions using models specific to industrial engineering and its corresponding specialty.
Work effectively in groups, integrating capacities and knowledge to make decisions in the field of industrial engineering and its corresponding specialty.
Raise awareness about the values of total quality, environment, and occupational risks.
Understand what quality is, what it is for, why it is necessary, and how it should be achieved in the company.
Understand environmental issues, why its protection is necessary, and how it should be achieved in the company.
Understand the importance of occupational risk prevention, why it is necessary, and how it should be achieved in the company.

syllabus_topics: The Development of Quality Management in Companies
Planning, training, and implementation of quality in companies
BLOCK 3. ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT AND OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY MANAGEMENT
BLOCK 4. RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN QUALITY MANAGEMENT, ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT, AND OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY MANAGEMENT: INTEGRATION OF MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS.
Quality, Environment, and Safety Management Systems or Models
OHSAS 18001 and ISO 45001 Occupational Risk Prevention Standard.
Possibilities for integrating the three systems. Advantages and disadvantages.

assessment_methods.method: Completion of practical exercises, cases or problems

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 (or proportional equivalent) is required for each activity and the written exam. If all minimums are met, the final grade is the weighted sum of all components (written exam 70%, practices 10%, team projects 20%). If any minimum is not met, the student fails the continuous assessment. Students can opt for a final assessment, which comprises an exam and global evaluation activities worth 100% of the grade. In the extraordinary call, students are evaluated solely through a final assessment, although positive results from the continuous assessment may be preserved at the professor's discretion.
